title: BepiColombo spacecraft enters orbit around Mercury after eight-year journey
dek: The European-Japanese BepiColombo spacecraft has successfully entered orbit around Mercury following an eight-year journey, despite experiencing a minor thruster issue during the insertion maneuver.
happened: On 21 November 2026, the European Space Agency and Japan Aerospace Exploration Agency joint mission BepiColombo successfully entered orbit around Mercury after an eight-year journey through the inner solar system. According to the European Space Agency, the spacecraft performed a critical orbit insertion maneuver by firing four chemical thrusters to slow its speed. During this maneuver, a software glitch caused the thruster burn to be shorter than planned. Flight controllers in Germany spent several hours reviewing telemetry before confirming the successful orbital capture. Launched in October 2018, the spacecraft traveled approximately 9.9 billion kilometers utilizing multiple planetary flybys of Earth, Venus, and Mercury. The mission's two linked orbiters remain connected while mission teams investigate the technical issue. The spacecraft entered an elliptical polar orbit measuring approximately 590 by 11,640 kilometers. The mission aims to examine Mercury's dense interior, magnetic field, impact craters, and volcanic plains.

sides.says: The European Space Agency confirmed the successful orbital arrival on November 21 and stated that the spacecraft remains safe while mission teams investigate a software-related problem that shortened the planned thruster firing duration.

Lead project scientist Geraint Jones stated that the team cannot wait for data to stream down in the spring, noting that the mission will provide "unprecedented measurements taken by two spacecraft at the planet at the same time."

next: The two scientific orbiters are scheduled to separate on December 9 and 10, 2026, with routine scientific operations expected to begin in April 2027.
summary: The European-Japanese BepiColombo spacecraft successfully entered orbit around Mercury following an eight-year journey. The joint mission of the European Space Agency and the Japan Aerospace Exploration Agency experienced a software glitch during its thruster burn insertion maneuver, prompting an investigation by mission controllers in Germany. The conjoined spacecraft, consisting of two scientific orbiters, will separate in December to study Mercury's surface, interior, and magnetic environment, with full scientific operations slated to begin in April 2027.
